cards.question: What is the difference between type I and type II error?
cards.answer: Type I (α) — false positive: rejecting a true null hypothesis. Set conventionally at 0.05. Type II (β) — false negative: failing to reject a false null hypothesis. Power = 1 − β, usually set at 0.8. Type I error is reduced by smaller α; Type II error by larger sample size or effect size.

cards.question: Explain absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction and number needed to treat.
cards.answer: ARR = control event rate − treatment event rate. RRR = ARR / control event rate. NNT = 1 / ARR. Example: mortality 10 % → 8 %. ARR = 2 %, RRR = 20 %, NNT = 50 (treat 50 patients to prevent one death). RRR alone exaggerates clinically small effects; always quote ARR and NNT.

cards.question: What is the difference between sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratio?
cards.answer: Sensitivity = true positives / (true positives + false negatives) — ability to detect disease. Specificity = true negatives / (true negatives + false positives) — ability to exclude disease. Likelihood ratio + = sensitivity / (1 − specificity); LR+ >10 strongly increases post-test probability. Unlike PPV/NPV, LRs are independent of disease prevalence.
